performance.title: Performance
performance.explanation: Performance is like a snapshot of your financial month: it's the difference between how much came in and how much went out. Income minus expenses (fixed, daily, savings, card and daily budget forecast) = performance.

economized.title: Saved
economized.explanation: This is the percentage you managed to save relative to everything that came in during the period. Ideally it should be between 20% and 30%.

costOfLiving.title: Cost of living
costOfLiving.loadError: Could not load the cost of living.
costOfLiving.explanation: Cost of living is how much you spend to live: expenses, daily spending, card spending and the daily budget forecast for the remaining days of the month.

dailyAverage.title: Daily average
dailyAverage.loadError: Could not load the daily average.
dailyAverage.explanation: It's the sum of all daily expenses (not counting future forecast) divided by the number of days in the month. This way you know, on average, how much you spend per day in your lifestyle.

widget.itemHint: Balance, daily budget and goal on your home screen
widget.title: iPhone widget
widget.intro: iPhone only shows widgets from native apps, so we use the free Scriptable app. The widget shows what you can still spend today, the month balance and goal progress.
widget.step1: Get it on the App Store:
widget.step2: The key is personal, read-only and can be revoked here at any time.
widget.step2Existing: You already have an active key. For safety it is not shown again; generate a new one to copy the script (the previous one stops working).
widget.step3: It already contains your key. Tap the button to copy it.
widget.step4Title: 4. Add it to Scriptable and your home screen
widget.step4: In Scriptable tap + and paste the script. Name it Zeno. Then on the home screen long-press an empty spot, tap +, pick Scriptable and a widget size, tap the widget and choose Zeno under Script.
widget.secret: Treat the script like a password: anyone with the key can see the summary. If it leaks, tap Revoke.

capture.itemHint: Apple Pay adds the expense for you
capture.title: Automatic spending (Apple Pay)
capture.intro: Every time you pay with a Wallet card (Apple Pay), the iPhone Shortcuts app can tell Zeno, which creates the Daily expense right away.
capture.step1: It is personal, can only create entries (it cannot read or delete anything) and can be revoked here.
capture.step1Existing: You already have an active key. For safety it is not shown again; generate a new one to see the fields (the previous one stops working).
capture.step2: In the Shortcuts app: Automation tab, tap +. In the trigger search (Automation chip), choose Wallet (called Transaction on older iOS). Select your cards and choose Run Immediately. Add the action Get Contents of URL.
capture.step3: Tap Show More and fill in. Method: POST. Request Body: JSON.
capture.step3Vars: In the title field, tap the value and pick the Merchant variable (Shortcut Input). In the amount field, pick the Amount variable. Names may vary slightly by iOS version.
capture.secret: Treat the key like a password: anyone with it can create entries in your account. If it leaks, tap Revoke.
capture.limits: Wallet payments (tap to pay and online Apple Pay purchases) are captured as a Daily expense for today. Pix, bank slips, cash withdrawals and physical-card purchases don't go through Wallet and stay manual. If Shortcuts repeats the same alert within 2 minutes, Zeno ignores the repeat.
capture.step3Extra: Optional: add two more Text fields. For card, pick Shortcut Input and the card property (something like Card or Pass). For category, pick the Category property. Skip any that isn't in the list. They go into the description and help choose the tag.
capture.rulesIntro: Zeno picks the spending tag on its own: first by the rules below (the text appears in the merchant name or category) and then by a tag with the same name as the Apple Pay category. With no match, the entry stays untagged.
capture.rulesNoTags: Create tags first (Tags menu) so you can link rules to them.
